# Generated by default (GN-01 to GN-06) and recording of rules (RG-01 to RG-04)

Rules for what the skill builds WITHOUT being asked, in every new project and every migration (owner request of 2026-11-14). They sit on top of the DS rules they name (AV, NT, BD, PC, UN, MO, AX, PR): those keep their text; these say that the feature must exist, who defines its content for the project, and how to prove it. Each rule has Rule, Meet and Check. Status: owner rules of 2026-11-14, recorded in the register of the DS repo as GN-01..06 and RG-01..04.

How to read "adapted to the project": derive the content from what the project really has (its entities, statuses, roles, workflows), never copy the example names of another product, and never invent data the project does not keep. When the project gives nothing to derive from, build the mechanism with the smallest honest content (one category, the signed-in user's own events) and say so in the hand-over report.

### GN-01
**Rule.** Every application has an **Activity history** item in the menu of the user (the avatar dropdown), under My preferences and above the divider and Sign out (AV-01, AV-04, NV-13), without the user asking for it. It opens a page (`#/mylog`) with the history of what the SIGNED-IN user did in the application: newest first (OR-01), grouped by day, one row per event with time, the action and its target, a category label and the note, using the existing History list item (`LogList`); a category filter and a search field when there are more than ten events. The application records an event through ONE function (`logActivity({ category, action, targetType, targetId, note })`) that every create, update, delete, approve, reject, publish, export and sign-in calls; the event is kept per account and holds business values only (NT-07). The categories are those of the project's own domain (for example Orders, Customers, Settings), three to six, defined once in `activity.config`; a reader with an audit permission may also see an Audit log page, which is a separate item.
**Meet.** The user menu has the item `data-testid="mylog"` with the icon `history`; the route exists in `nav.config`; the page is a List pattern page (TB-17); every mutating handler of the project calls `logActivity`; the empty state says that nothing was done yet instead of showing an Alert (CD-08).
**Check.** Open the user menu: the item is there in the right place. Do one create, one edit and one delete in the project and see three rows, newest first. Search the code for a mutating handler (`create`, `update`, `delete`, `approve`) that does not call `logActivity`.

### GN-02
**Rule.** Every application has **Notifications**, built without being asked, in the form the DS defines (NT-01 to NT-12): a bell with the unread count in the action row of the sidebar (or the toolbar, PP-01), a dropdown with the latest items and "Mark all as read", "View all notifications" opening a drawer with the last three months and category tabs. The CATEGORIES and the KINDS are defined for the project in `notifications.config` from its own workflows: list the events people must act on or know about (something waiting for my decision, something assigned to me, something overdue or expiring, something that failed, a result that finished), group them into three to five categories named in the project's language of work (the DS example uses Rules, Data and Work), and give each kind: its category, who receives it (by role or by ownership), its title and summary in English and Indonesian, and the page it opens. Every kind belongs to exactly one category (NT-10). Notifications are DERIVED on render from the records the application already keeps (NT-03); the only stored thing is the read state, per account (NT-04). Business values only, never personal or medical detail (NT-07). Opening a page shows no Alert, toast or request because of notifications (NT-08).
**Meet.** `notifications.config` exists with the categories, the kinds, the audiences and both languages; the bell is in the shell; the drawer tabs are the categories plus All; a project without any workflow to notify about still gets the bell, the dropdown and the drawer with the empty state ("You are all caught up").
**Check.** Count the kinds in the config and the tabs in the drawer: every kind is under one category and every category has a tab. Mark one as read, reload: it stays read; sign in as another account: it is unread there. Search the config for a kind without an audience or without both languages.

### GN-03
**Rule.** Every badge explains itself in a tooltip on hover, keyboard focus and tap, automatically (BD-13): "<what it is> is <label>" (Status is Active, Priority is High). The project never writes the sentence by hand per badge: a badge takes its meaning from ONE central map of the project (`badgeProps(domain, value)`: the domain name, the value, the intent, the icon), and the `Badge` and `DotBadge` components build the tooltip from it. A new status, category or level is added to the map, never to a page. A label that is only a number, a name or a value the user chose is not a badge (BD-10) and gets no tooltip.
**Meet.** In React every `Badge` has `domain` + `value`, or `what`, or `tip`; in HTML the `badge()` helper is called with the same; the central map covers every status and category of the project's entities; the tooltip is the Tooltip bubble (dark with a tail), not `title=`.
**Check.** Hover a badge in each table and each detail page: a bubble appears. Search for `<Badge` without `domain`, `what` or `tip`, for a class `bdg` written as raw markup, and for a `title=` used as the explanation of a badge.

### GN-04
**Rule.** Every place that shows the NAME OF A USER of the application (an owner, assignee, creator, approver, reviewer, last editor, a staff member in a table cell, a history row, a comment, a card) shows it as the trigger of the **profile card** (UN-01, PC-01 to PC-04), automatically: the project uses the one component `UserName` (React) or `userName()` (HTML) for every user name and never prints a bare name. The card is a non-modal popover (PC-02): it opens on hover after a short delay, on keyboard focus and on tap, closes with Escape and keeps the focus on the trigger. The FIELDS of the card are defined for the project in `profile.config` from its own user directory: the avatar with initials, the name, a subtitle (the position or the role), and three to five rows the project really keeps for a user (for example unit or branch, email, phone, status, last active, number of open items). The card shows no field the viewer may not see (PC-05) and never a government identifier unmasked. A customer, a member or any other entity the project shows by name may get its own card variant by the same pattern, defined in the same file.
**Meet.** `profile.config` exists; the component is used in tables, detail pages, history rows and cards; the name has no underline in any state (UN-01) and the same font as the text around it; the signed-in user's own name in the menu and a name inside another interactive control are the documented exceptions.
**Check.** Hover, focus (Tab) and tap a user name in a table, a detail page and the activity history: the card opens; Escape closes it. Search the pages for a user name printed as plain text from a record (`row.owner`, `createdBy`, `assignee`).

### GN-05
**Rule.** The **motion rules run by themselves** in everything the project builds (MO-01 to MO-07, AX-02), with no extra work per page: the page content fades in over `--dur-page`; the numbers of stat cards and KPIs count up once (`animate` is left on); the first rows of a table fade in; a new or changed row glows (`mo-new`); popovers, dropdowns, toasts, drawers and dialogs enter with the DS animation; buttons press in; a wizard step line draws and a done screen pops. All of it comes from the design-system stylesheets and components, so the project adds NO keyframes, transitions or durations of its own: a project animation that is needed uses `--dur-fast`, `--dur-base`, `--dur-slow` and `--ease-out`, moves only opacity, transform and colour, and never loops except a status pulse (BD-01). Motion stands still, and the final screen is shown at once, when the system asks for reduced motion and in automated browsers (MO-03, through `data-motion="off"` on the root).
**Meet.** The root element sets `data-motion` from the motion setting of the starter (`motionOff()`); the project CSS has no `transition` or `animation` with a literal time or easing; the stat cards, tables and overlays of the project are the DS components.
**Check.** Open a list page: the content fades in and the stat numbers count up. Switch the system to reduced motion: nothing moves. Run the audit: no `transition:` or `animation:` with a literal `ms` or `s` value outside the design-system folder, and no `@keyframes` outside it.

### GN-06
**Rule.** **Remove what is not needed any more, in the same piece of work.** When a request, a migration or a new page replaces something, the thing it replaces is deleted, not left behind or commented out: the starter example pages and routes (`ex-*`, the Examples menu entry) once the real pages exist; a menu entry, route, page, component, hook, style, i18n key, mock record, image and test that nothing uses any more; an old copy of a component the design system now provides (the project's own badge, tooltip, date input, select, modal); `TODO` placeholders and demo text of the starter; and the dead branches and commented-out blocks of what was touched. A removal never changes the design system files or a rule, and a thing the owner asked to keep is not removed (PR-03: what the owner removed stays removed). The removals are listed in the hand-over report and in `docs/design-system/changelog.md`.
**Meet.** After the change, a search for the name of each removed thing finds nothing; `npm run typecheck` (or the build) passes; `node scripts/check-texts.mjs` reports no key used but missing; no file is left that nothing imports.
**Check.** For every item you replaced, search the project for its name, its route, its class and its i18n keys. Run the typecheck and the text check. Look for commented-out code in the files you touched and for files that no module imports.

## Recording of rules (RG-01 to RG-04)

The same four rules apply to the project you build: it keeps its own register `docs/design-system/rules-register.md` (a copy is in each starter), next to `changelog.md` and `new-components.md`.

### RG-01
**Rule.** Every rule the owner of the project gives (in a prompt, in chat or in an image) and every rule you create on your own (a default you generate, an audit or tooling decision, a content choice that others will have to follow) is written in the register of the project in the same piece of work: id (two to four capital letters, a dash, two digits), the rule in one sentence, the source (who, when), the kind, the status, the test or check that guards it, and the date. A rule that lives only in a conversation, a comment or this skill does not exist for the project. The project's `README` or `CLAUDE.md` says so.
**Meet.** `docs/design-system/rules-register.md` exists in the project; a new rule is in it before the work is reported done; its guard is a test, a script or a named manual check.
**Check.** Open the register: every rule given in this piece of work is there with source and guard. Search the code for comments that state a rule ("always", "never", "must") that the register does not have.

### RG-02
**Rule.** A new or changed rule that contradicts a rule that already exists (in the register of the project or in this skill) is reported to the owner at once, in the same reply and before anything is built on it: name both rules, say what clashes, record the new one as `perlu keputusan owner` (pending the owner) in the Konflik section, and leave the existing rule active and unchanged until the owner decides. Never settle a conflict by relaxing a check, picking a side or building both. Run `node scripts/rules-conflicts.mjs --new <ids>` for every new rule: it lists hard conflicts (a rule that says it replaces another that is still active) and candidates (two rules that share terms and forbid and require the same thing, or give different values).
**Meet.** The reply starts with the conflict; the register has the pending row and the Konflik entry; no code depends on the new rule yet.
**Check.** Run the script after adding rules: no hard conflict; every candidate is explained or reported.

### RG-03
**Rule.** The skill and the Praisindo register stay in step: a rule is published in the skill only after it is in the register of the Praisindo DS; at each update of the skill every register id is classified (general, domain, exception) and every id the skill carries exists in the register; the skill number equals the DS number. The procedure is `docs/design-system/skill-sync.md` of the DS repo (`scripts/rules-coverage.mjs --triage <table> --register <register>`).
**Meet.** The coverage run with the triage table and the register has no NOT TRIAGED, UNKNOWN or MISSING line, or each remaining line is listed to the owner as sync debt.
**Check.** Run it and read the output.

### RG-04
**Rule.** A rule or decision you create on your own is never active by itself: it is recorded as `perlu keputusan owner` with the reason it was made and waits in the Konflik section until the owner confirms it (it then gets a check and becomes active) or rejects it (it is removed). Tell the owner about it in the report of the piece of work that made it.
**Meet.** Every default, relaxation or threshold you chose is in the register as pending and in the report.
**Check.** Search the report and the tool files for a threshold, an exception or a default that has no row.
